summary.one_liner: A long, opinionated list of web and software development lessons from nearly 25 years of practice, covering HTML-first design, CSS layering, SPAs, dependencies, build tools, management, and product strategy.
takeaways: Prefer HTML-first, progressively enhanced pages that work without CSS or JS, and keep SPAs to cases that truly need them.
Layer CSS (variables, base, layout, blocks, utilities) and avoid !important and ID selectors; style state with data-* attributes.
Minimise build steps and dependencies, since each adds cost, security risk, and loss of team understanding of the codebase.
Treat software as a living ecosystem rather than a project, and value code-quality work and structured communication.
Use shared context, naming, and undo-friendly design so users can build a mental map and recover from mistakes.
summary.summary: This is a personal list by Baldur Bjarnason of 136 opinionated statements about web development, written as a single long post from about a week of distilling his experience. The points are short, numbered-style assertions with minimal explanation, and cover topics such as failure demand, UX and screen usage, SPA pitfalls and history handling, CSS architecture, feedback loops and build tooling, dependencies, team management, and business strategy. The author states up front that he does not explain the points, so the value lies in the claims themselves rather than worked examples. The page text provided ends mid-list in the business section.
